name: Executive Order of October 16, 1891 extending the Hoopa Valley Reservation to the Klamath River (the "Addition")
citation: Executive Order of October 16, 1891 (President Benjamin Harrison), under the Act of April 8, 1864
promises: Not a treaty. The President extended the Hoopa Valley Reservation to include a strip one mile wide on each side of the Klamath River from its limits to the Pacific (Royce).
The Supreme Court records that the order brought the old Klamath River Reservation and the connecting strip into the Hoopa Valley Reservation (Mattz v. Arnett, 1973).
today: Congress ordered the original Klamath River Reservation sold by the Act of June 17, 1892, but the Supreme Court held in Mattz v. Arnett (1973) that the Act did not end the reservation. The Hoopa-Yurok Settlement Act of 1988 made the 1891 Addition the Yurok Reservation and the 1876 square the Hoopa Valley Reservation; the Federal Circuit held in Karuk Tribe v. Ammon (2000) that the executive orders gave no compensable property rights.

openQuestions: This order added land; no finding that it was broken was found. The 1892 Act concerns the Klamath River Reservation (cession-1855-11-16-klamath, Royce 400).

treaties.json lists only the Hoopa Valley Tribe; since 1988 the Addition is the Yurok Reservation, so the Yurok Tribe should be listed. Its royce link points to p. 832 (the 1864 entry); the 1891 entry is on p. 942. Noted, not edited.
Neither tribe's own account of the 1891 order was located in this pass.
